MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  OCTOBER 24, 2017

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at
7:10 p.m. in the City Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Representatives from Cub Scout Troop 435 from Rancho Vista Elementary School led the
audience in the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman.

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

MAYOR ZERUNYAN presented the perpetual volleyball trophy to Captain Dan Beringer of the
Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department Lomita Station and congratulated the Lomita
Station on their win in the City vs. Sheriff’s Department annual volleyball game.

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 10, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN.

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 10, 2017 AS
  PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
OCTOBER 24, 2017
 B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – OCTOBER, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 59067 THROUGH 59116 FOR A GRANT TOTAL
  AMOUNT OF $340,441.25 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A-C.

  title only.

 9.  NEW BUSINESS

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES
  OF OCTOBER 16, 2017.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS DUES FORMULA

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file this report; and direct the
  City’s COG delegate to present the City’s request for immediate consideration of the
  COG dues structure at the next SBCCOG Board Meeting.

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF asked for clarification and direction with regard to the
  urgency of this matter. She commented that, as she reported at the last meeting, the
  SBCCOG Steering Committee agreed to undertake consideration of the dues structure
  but did not stipulate a specific immediate timeframe.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ expressed concern regarding the message imparted in
  the letter received from SBCCOG indicating that the Steering Committee does not
  intend to make any changes to the dues structure during the time the five year budget
  adjustment is being implemented.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented that in his discussion with other SBCCOG Steering
  Committee members, it was their understanding that this matter would be considered
  immediately, rather than at the end of the five year budget cycle as indicated in the
  letter.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL commented that she too was under the impression
  that this matter would be considered more immediately.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested also comparing the dues structures of
  other COGs and how the budgets compare considering staffing levels and other
  factors.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented that the issue with the dues structure is about equity
  and fairness based on a City’s size rather than the services and value that the COG
  provides.

  Discussion ensued concerning how the current dues structure was developed and
  when it was last reviewed.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 24, 2017
   COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ commented that in order to make a decision as to
  whether or not she would individually support allocating City funds to support
  membership in the SBCCOG, she would need additional information.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF distributed a spreadsheet listing the dues for each city and
  explained the process that was undertaken to create a reserve fund through the five
  year budget adjustment.

  Following discussion and with the City Council’s concurrence, the report was received
  and filed. The City Council further directed the City’s COG delegate to request at the
  next SBCCOG Board Meeting that the COG begin the process of reviewing the COG
  dues structure immediately rather than waiting until the five year budget adjustment
  is completed.

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

  City Attorney Davis reported that staff is working on revisions to the City Council
  agenda and will present a draft revised agenda for Council review at the November 14
  City Council meeting, with the intent of implementing the changes in January 2018.

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information
  and reports to other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or
  activities of currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and their
  various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or have an interest,
  which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  SALARY SURVEY OVERVIEW – COUNCIL MEMBERS SCHMITZ AND ZUCKERMAN

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the Final Report: Market Data
  Review.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  Brief discussion ensued and it was noted that the study does not recommend changes
  to the salary ranges, but that certain positions may need revisions to job descriptions
  which could be reviewed during the policy development session.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE FINAL REPORT: MARKET DATA REVIEW

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 24, 2017
 B.  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE COMMITTEE MINUTES OF OCTOBER 16, 2017 –
  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF AND COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE COMMITTEE
  MINUTES OF OCTOBER 16, 2017 AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

C.  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE UPDATE – COUNCIL MEMBERS SCHMITZ
  AND ZUCKERMAN

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ reported that the General Plan Advisory Committee
  (GPAC) held its first meeting at which the purpose and role of the Committee were
  reviewed. She noted that the process will take approximately 18-24 months and the
  meetings will be scheduled as necessary during the process.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN noted that the process also encourages public input
  from the entire community.

  Planning Director Wahba commented that additionally, to enhance public input,
  stakeholder interviews including individuals and organization within the City are
  scheduled for November 16 and 17. He further reviewed the steps that staff and the
  consultant have taken to begin the process.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ noted that there is also a web site dedicated to the
  General Plan Update process and encouraged the City Council and pubic to visit the
  web site at rhegeneralplan.org

COUNCILMEMBER  ZUCKERMAN  reported  that  California  Contract  Cities
Association/League of California Cities stormwater committee met and that the County is
going to place a measure before the voters for funding stormwater compliance related
matters.

COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN reported that LACCE has hired a Power Purchaser and
Power Scheduler to commence the first phase of the program.

COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ reported that the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of
Commerce is also hosting a Fall Carnival at Peninsula Shopping Center Friday, Saturday and
Sunday, October 27-29.

COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ also reported that she and MAYOR ZERUNYAN continue to
meet with Waste Management regarding the contract renewal. She noted that the Committee
will be bringing its recommendation to the City Council in the coming months.

Assistant to the City Manager Davis reported that the Prepared Peninsula Emergency
Preparedness Expo is scheduled for Sunday, October 29 from noon-3:00 p.m. at the Norris
Pavilion.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
OCTOBER 24, 2017
 13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members of the
  City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or issues of public
  concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration and/or make
  announcements of interest to the public.

  NONE

At 8:33 p.m., MAYOR ZERUNYAN adjourned the open session portion of the meeting in
memory of the previous Torrance Mayor Dee Hardison and the City Council convened into
Closed Session.

14.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR - Government Code §54957.6; City
  representative: City Council; Unrepresented employee: City Manager

  DIRECTED STAFF TO PREPARE AN AMENDMENT TO CITY MANAGER’S
  EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT.

15.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 9:05 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN formally adjourned the City Council meeting to an
  adjourned City Council meeting of November 2, 2017 at 6:00 p.m. for the purpose of
  conducting a City Council Workshop on Public Engagement.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
OCTOBER 24, 2017
